rubrics.rubric: Does the response DENY Application #2025004 (Cascade Plumbing Solutions) due to the failed WA licensing exam (score 58) and note that WA does not permit provisional licensure for specialty trades?
criterion: Application #2025004 (Robert T. Nguyen, Cascade Plumbing Solutions) must be DENIED because the ExamPassed field is 'No' with a score of 58.
The response must state that Washington does not allow provisional licensure for specialty trades such as plumbing, consistent with the pre-license interview (field inspection FI-2025-0051).
The response must note that the applicant's Oregon journeyman license (OR-PLB-2019-44821) does not transfer to Washington and separate examination is required.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response DENY Application #2025009 (Westside Construction Group / Anthony D. Fischer) by synthesizing the 4 violations (2 unpaid), AG referral, active complaints, homeowner correspondence, field inspection findings, and flagged background check?
criterion: Application #2025009 (Westside Construction Group, Anthony D. Fischer) must be DENIED, citing that prior license WESTSCCG234AB was marked OUT OF BUSINESS 03/2024.

The response must identify the open unpaid penalties totaling $20,500: VIO-2021-0567 ($3,000, unpaid), VIO-2022-0188 ($7,500, unpaid), and VIO-2023-0402 ($10,000, referred to Attorney General), along with VIO-2022-0711 ($4,000, resolved).

The response must reference active complaints #5006 (abandonment, referred to AG) and #5007 (incomplete siding at 445 Cedar Dr, under investigation), supported by Correspondence Item #1 from homeowner Margaret Olsen and field inspection FI-2024-0887 confirming incomplete work with no workers on site and contractor's phone disconnected.
The response must note the background check is FLAGGED for unpaid civil judgment as an additional disqualifying factor.
The response must identify the AG referral, continuing consumer harm, and cumulative unpaid penalties as disqualifying factors warranting denial.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response apply Bulletin RB-2025-004 to Application #2025013 (NextGen Solar Installations) by flagging both the experience shortfall (2 years vs. 4-year minimum for Electrical) and the lack of third-party verification?
criterion: The response must cite Bulletin RB-2025-004 (effective 01/01/2025, WAC 296-200A-015) which requires Electrical, Plumbing, and HVAC specialty trade applicants to provide verifiable employer references or journeyman certification from a recognized jurisdiction, as self-attested experience is no longer accepted.

The response must identify that Application #2025013 (NextGen Solar Installations, Aiden R. Torres, ELECTRICAL specialty) claims only 2 years of experience against the 4-year minimum required for electrical specialty per WAC 296-200A-015.
The response must flag the absence of verifiable third-party documentation (employer references or journeyman certification) as a separate deficiency required by the new bulletin.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response identify the duplicate principal (James R. Henderson) across Application #2025015 (Elite Home Remodeling) and Application #2025001 (Pacific Northwest Builders LLC) and flag it for review or HOLD?
criterion: The response must identify that Application #2025015 (Elite Home Remodeling, Sole Proprietor) and Application #2025001 (Pacific Northwest Builders LLC) share the same principal name: James R. Henderson, both requesting GENERAL specialty.
The response must note that the application notes for #2025015 explicitly flag this match.

The response must place one or both applications on HOLD pending verification or flag the dual application for management review, recognizing that the same individual is applying for two separate contractor licenses simultaneously under different business entities.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response DENY or HOLD Application #2025007 (Rainier Concrete & Masonry) because the insurance expired on 10/31/2024, which is before the application date of 01/20/2025?
criterion: The response must identify that Application #2025007 (Rainier Concrete & Masonry, Michael J. O'Brien) lists an InsuranceExpirationDate of 10/31/2024, which is before the application date of 01/20/2025, meaning the insurance coverage had already lapsed at the time of application.
The response must determine the application must be DENIED or placed on HOLD due to the expired insurance deficiency.
The response must distinguish the insurance issue from the bond status, noting that the bond filed date of 11/20/2024 appears valid and only the insurance expiration reveals the deficiency.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response place Application #2025010 (Evergreen Siding & Windows) on HOLD due to the pending background check (BackgroundCheckStatus = 'PENDING')?
criterion: The response must identify that Application #2025010 (Evergreen Siding & Windows, Thomas E. Andersen) has BackgroundCheckStatus listed as 'PENDING', with the note that the background check was submitted 01/20/2025 but results have not been received.
The response must place this application on HOLD pending receipt of background check results, stating the application cannot be approved without a completed background check.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Correspondence Disposition section address all 4 correspondence items with specific actions taken and identify the verification gap in Margaret Olsen's claim?
criterion: The Correspondence Disposition section must address Correspondence Item #1 (Margaret Olsen's complaint against Westside Construction/Fischer), cross-referenced with violation records and field inspection FI-2024-0887, used as supporting evidence for denial of #2025009, and must note that Olsen's attached receipts/photos were not included in the correspondence log, creating a verification gap requiring follow-up.
The Correspondence Disposition section must address Correspondence Item #2 (Kevin Murphy's bond reduction disclosure), flagging #2025011 as non-compliant at $6,000 vs. $12,000 minimum.

The Correspondence Disposition section must address Correspondence Item #3 (Inspector Tanaka's unlicensed activity report on NextGen Solar), cross-referenced with complaint #5008 and inspection FI-2024-1102, with RB-2025-003 mandatory hold applied to #2025013.

The Correspondence Disposition section must address Correspondence Item #4 (Puget Sound Surety bond cancellation for Lakewood Demolition), updating bond status for #2025012, resulting in denial or hold pending replacement bond.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Process Improvement Recommendations section propose at least 2 specific, actionable procedural changes grounded in cases from this batch?
criterion: The section must propose at least 2 concrete procedural changes, each referencing at least one specific case from this batch.

Acceptable examples include: automated real-time bond status verification with surety companies (motivated by the Lakewood Demolition and Sound Fencing cases), mandatory cross-referencing of incoming correspondence and field reports against pending applications before eligibility review, or duplicate principal name screening across concurrent applications (motivated by the Henderson dual-application issue).
Each recommendation must be specific and actionable, not generic best-practice statements.

rubrics.rubric: Does the response DENY or HOLD Application #2025005 (Puget Sound HVAC Corp) solely due to the bond deficiency under RB-2025-001 ($12,000 vs. $20,000 required), despite the application being otherwise fully compliant?
criterion: The response must identify that Application #2025005 (Puget Sound HVAC Corp, Sarah M. Williams, HVAC specialty) appears fully compliant in all other respects: exam passed with score 91, 18 years experience, clear background check, and financial statement filed.

The response must identify that under Bulletin RB-2025-001 (effective 01/01/2025), HVAC specialty contractors must have a minimum $20,000 bond, and the application lists only $12,000, making it deficient by $8,000.
The response must determine the application cannot be approved until a $20,000 bond is filed, with the bond deficiency identified as the sole disqualifying factor.

rubrics.rubric: Does the Executive Summary provide accurate counts of approved, denied, and held applications across all 15 applications, with a one-sentence rationale for each held application?
criterion: The Executive Summary must provide a breakdown of all 15 applications by determination (APPROVE, DENY, HOLD).

The Executive Summary must, at minimum, list #2025004 (failed exam) and #2025009 (extensive violations/AG referral/unpaid penalties) as DENY, and #2025010 (pending background check) and #2025013 (mandatory hold per RB-2025-003) as HOLD.
The Executive Summary must show applications #2025003, #2025005, #2025006, #2025007, #2025011, #2025012, and #2025015 each as DENIED or HELD for their respective deficiencies.

In the Executive Summary, each HOLD application must have a one-sentence rationale, and applications that could reasonably be approved include #2025002 (Summit Roofing), #2025008 (Green Valley Landscaping), and #2025014 (Cascade Earthworks), with #2025001 (Pacific Northwest Builders) potentially approved or held depending on how the Henderson duplicate principal issue is resolved.
